audit.whatIsWrong: Four of seven chart rows disagreed across layers: phases[3..5].side read 'Skill' and phases[6].side read 'Ryze', while win[3..6] all read 'Irelia'.
audit.why: The packet levelChart reads Irelia on all seven rows, the content whys argue Irelia at every stage, and the full-layer whys under those Skill/Ryze sides also described Irelia winning — the sides were the outlier, and row 6 in particular said Ryze above a sentence about Irelia surfing the fight.
audit.corrected: phases[3..6].side moved to Irelia, matching win[] and the packet, with each why rewritten to argue that verdict from Ryze's real cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was described as an 'ult wall locks him down before he can chain snares to escape', implying Realm Warp is an escape.
audit.why: Realm Warp is a 3000-range portal on 180/160/140s that teleports allies standing near it after a delay. It repositions his team; it is not a personal escape and it does nothing about a stun that has already landed.
audit.corrected: Stated in whys[4], phases[4].why, mid and breakdown.carry.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three mechanical errors. The text repeatedly calls Ryze's E a 'snare' ('his E snare', 'root-snare-root chain', 'once E-snared'). It describes his passive as a 'burn' he 'stacks'. And it tells you to use Defiant Dance to blunt his damage.
audit.why: Spell Flux (E) is a debuff on 3.5-to-2.5s; it applies Flux and roots nothing. Rune Prison (W) is the lockdown at 615 range on 11-to-9s, and per Riot's own text it SLOWS unless the target already has Flux, in which case it roots instead. Arcane Mastery is bonus damage from bonus mana, not a burn. And Defiant Dance reduces physical damage — Ryze's damage is magic, so the W does not blunt his burst. That last one is the decisive interaction of the matchup and the page currently advises the opposite.
audit.corrected: Flux-then-root sequence named throughout; the physical-only limit on Defiant Dance written into phases[1].why, dosFull[1].d and early.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d called Rune Prison a 'fifteen-second invitation'; breakdown.cooldowns had no digit at all.
audit.why: Rune Prison is 11s at rank 1 and 9s at rank 5. Fifteen seconds would send a player in six seconds late.
audit.corrected: Real numbers given in dosFull[2].d, breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.feeding and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two copy-paste bleeds: dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d carried the tradeGood/tradeBad strings under unrelated titles.
audit.corrected: Both replaced with bodies matching their titles.

edits.before: At level 1-2 Ryze wants to sit at max range poking with Q while stacking his passive burn, so Irelia should shove the wave and use minions to dash into range without eating a free trade. Irelia's early trades are strong once she's on top of him since Ryze has almost nothing to punish melee proximity outside a root. Watch for his E snare in melee range and use W's parry to neutralize a follow-up auto. If Ryze wastes mana poking, punish the lull with a full combo.
edits.after: At levels 1-2 Ryze sits at max range poking with Overload, so shove the wave and use minions to dash into range without eating a free trade. Your early trades are strong once you are on top of him, since the only thing punishing melee proximity is Rune Prison at 615 — and that cage only roots if Spell Flux is already on you. Dodge the orb and the root is a slow. Defiant Dance cuts physical damage, so don't count on it against his magic; punish the lull once he has burnt mana poking.

edits.before: By level 3-5 Irelia should keep closing the gap every wave since Ryze has no way to disengage once she's stacked passive on him. His level 6 ult lets him reposition but doesn't stop Irelia's dash chain onto minions, and Vanguard's Edge can lock him down before he even roots. Track his snare cooldown carefully — it's his only real defensive tool in melee range, and once it's down he's fully exposed to an all-in.
edits.after: By levels 3-5 keep closing the gap every wave, since Ryze has no dash and no disengage once you are stacked on him. Realm Warp at level 6 is a 3000-range portal on 180 seconds that repositions his team; it does not stop your dash chain onto minions, and Vanguard's Edge marks him before he can set up the root. Track Rune Prison — 9 seconds at rank 5, his only defensive tool in melee range — and once it is down he is fully exposed.

notes: The most important correction here is not a name: the page told the reader to use Defiant Dance to absorb Ryze's burst. Irelia's W reduces PHYSICAL damage per Riot's text and Ryze's damage is magic, so that advice actively loses trades. I rewrote phases[1].why, dosFull[1].d and early to say so, but breakdown.wave and the report entries still carry the generic 'W the burst' framing and I left those alone rather than expand scope. Also corrected: Ryze's E was called a snare in four places (Spell Flux is a debuff; Rune Prison is the lockdown, and it only roots when Flux is already applied — otherwise it slows), and his passive was called a stacking burn (Arcane Mastery is bonus damage from bonus mana). Chart: rows 3-6 disagreed across layers and I moved the full-layer sides to Irelia to match win[] and the packet; no win[N] edits were needed because the content values were already right. Not verified from the kits: whether Rune Prison's root can be cleansed or shortened by tenacity, and whether Irelia's Bladesurge dash can be used to leave the Rune Prison root once applied.
